title: Frontend Coding & Implementation Standards

allowed_stack_scope.styling: Vanilla CSS3 using custom properties (variables) for visual tokens.
allowed_stack_scope.client_logic: Vanilla ES6+ JavaScript modules running directly in modern web browsers.
allowed_stack_scope.prohibitions: No TypeScript, no Node.js build steps, no webpack/vite bundles, no frontend frameworks (React, Vue, Angular), no CSS frameworks (Tailwind, Bootstrap).

js/.modules/: Core system modules (auth, packages, reservation, scheduling, customization, inventory, payments, equipment, reports, audit)

javascript_coding_rules: Use native ES modules (import/export). Avoid global window scope.
Naming conventions: camelCase for vars/funcs, UPPER_SNAKE_CASE for constants/enums, PascalCase for classes/modules, snake_case for database fields.
Business calculations MUST exist in exactly one authoritative utility module.
Explicit try/catch error handling required for all async operations. No silent catch blocks.
User inputs MUST be sanitized and validated against shared data types before API calls.
Use comments to explain business constraints, not obvious code syntax.
security_hygiene: Never place private API keys, service credentials, or secrets in frontend JS or HTML files.
Treat all frontend JS as publicly inspectable on GitHub Pages.
Enforce access control in backend Firebase Security Rules.
refactoring_policy: Edit ONLY files within the assigned task's module scope. Do NOT perform unrequested refactoring in shared code or unrelated modules.
